pages.c07-p01: Explain how web pages are created using Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), including the html, head and body structure
pages.c07-p02: Describe the purpose of common HTML tags: paragraph, headings, line break, image, anchor (hyperlink), ordered list and unordered list
pages.c07-p03: Describe the purpose of tag attributes, empty and container tags, character entities and simple tables and forms
pages.c07-p04: Explain how Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) are used to control the presentation of web pages, using selectors, properties and values
pages.c07-p05: Compare inline, internal (global) and external style sheets and explain how inheritance and precedence resolve style conflicts
pages.c07-p06: Explain the benefits of separating content (HTML) from presentation (CSS)
pages.c07-p07: Describe how a website is planned, including purpose, target audience, site maps and storyboards
pages.c07-p08: Describe linear, hierarchical and non-linear navigation structures and principles of usability
pages.c07-p09: Explain how websites can be made accessible, with reference to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)
pages.c07-p10: Distinguish between static web pages and web applications, and between client-side and server-side processing
pages.c07-p11: Explain why form input should be validated both on the client and on the server
pages.c07-p12: Describe how a website is tested, published and maintained

q.q: What is the main job of HTML?
o: To set the colours, fonts and layout of each page
To mark up the content so the browser knows what each part is
To run scripts on the web server before a page is sent
To store the site's data in tables for later queries
q.why: HTML describes structure and meaning; presentation is CSS's job.

q.q: What is an HTML element?
o: An opening tag, its content and the matching closing tag together
A keyword written inside angle brackets with no content
A name="value" pair written inside the opening tag
A rule made of a selector followed by declarations
q.why: Tags mark up content; the opening tag, content and closing tag form an element. name="value" is an attribute.

q.q: Nested HTML elements must be closed in which order?
o: In the same order as they were opened
In alphabetical order of their tag names
In the reverse order to which they were opened
In any order, as long as all are closed
q.why: The most recently opened element must be closed first.

q.q: Which section of an HTML page contains the content displayed in the browser window?
o: head
title
meta
body
q.why: The body holds everything the user sees.

q.q: Which of these belongs in the head section of an HTML page?
o: The link to the page's style sheet
The main h1 heading of the page
The paragraphs of text on the page
The table of fixture results
q.why: The head holds information about the page: title, character set, style sheet links, scripts and metadata.

q.q: Where is the text shown on the browser tab defined?
o: In an h1 element in the body
In the title element in the head
In the lang attribute of the html element
In the external CSS file
q.why: The title element sets the tab text; a visible heading needs h1.

q.q: What does the browser do with several spaces, tabs and new lines typed in the HTML source?
o: Displays every one of them exactly
Starts a new paragraph for each new line
Reports a syntax error in the page
Treats them as a single space
q.why: White space collapses to one space, so indentation is just for human readers.

q.q: Why does the html element have a lang attribute such as lang="en-GB"?
o: It tells the browser the page uses the HTML5 standard
It sets the character set so that accented letters display
It states the page's language for screen readers and search engines
It chooses the spelling used by CSS properties such as color
q.why: The DOCTYPE declares HTML5 and the meta tag sets the character set.

q.q: Which tag creates a numbered list?
o: ul
li
nl
ol
q.why: ol is an ordered list, numbered automatically; ul gives bullets and li marks each item.

q.q: Which attribute of the anchor tag holds the destination of the link?
o: src
href
alt
link
q.why: href is the hypertext reference; src gives an image's file.

q.q: Which tag moves text onto a new line without starting a new paragraph?
o: br
p
hr
h1
q.why: br is a line break and is an empty tag.

q.q: Why should every img have an alt attribute?
o: It makes the image into a hyperlink to a larger version
It compresses the image so the page loads more quickly
It gives a text alternative read by screen readers and shown if the image fails
It sets the width and height of the image on screen
q.why: Alt text is essential for accessibility.

q.q: A list of kit is currently bulleted. What must change to make it numbered?
o: Each li tag is changed to an ol tag
A number is typed in front of each li item
The ul tags are changed to nl tags
Only the outer ul tags are changed to ol
q.why: The li items stay the same; only the list container changes.

q.q: Which href would link to another page called join.html in the same folder of the same site?
o: https://join.html
join.html
#join.html
mailto:join.html
q.why: A relative address names the file; https:// starts an absolute address, # jumps within a page and mailto: opens an email.

q.q: How can an image be made into a clickable link?
o: Place the img tag inside an anchor element
Add an href attribute to the img tag
Place the anchor tag inside the img element
Give the image an alt attribute
q.why: The enclosed content of an anchor, text or image, is what the user clicks.

q.q: What does the attribute type="I" do on an ol element?
o: Numbers the items with capital letters
Shows the list in italic text
Numbers the items with Roman numerals
Changes it into a bulleted list
q.why: type="A" gives capital letters and type="I" gives Roman numerals.

q.q: Which is an empty tag?
o: a
img
p
li
q.why: img has no closing tag and encloses nothing; the others are container tags.

q.q: Which list contains only container tags?
o: br, img, link, input
p, br, a, li
table, meta, ul, hr
p, h1, a, ul
q.why: br, img, link, input, meta and hr are empty tags.

q.q: Where are attributes written?
o: Inside the opening tag, as name="value"
Inside the closing tag, as name="value"
In a separate file linked from the head
Between the opening and closing tags
q.why: For example, href on a, or src and alt on img.

q.q: How does every HTML character entity begin and end?
o: It begins with a hash and ends with a colon
It begins with a less-than sign and ends with a greater-than sign
It begins with an ampersand and ends with a semicolon
It begins with a backslash and ends with a full stop
q.why: For example, the entity for the copyright sign is written ampersand, copy, semicolon.

q.q: Which entity displays an ampersand?
o: <
&
∧
q.why: & shows &; < shows a less-than sign and   a non-breaking space.

q.q: In an HTML table, what is the difference between th and td?
o: th is a table row; td is a cell inside that row
th is the table's caption; td is a header cell
th starts the table body; td starts the table head
th is a header cell (bold and centred by default); td is a data cell
q.why: tr is a row, th a header cell, td a data cell.

q.q: In a form, what does the action attribute specify?
o: The text shown on the submit button
The server-side script that receives the data
Whether the data is sent in the URL or the request body
The type of control the input displays
q.why: action names where the data goes; method sets how it is sent.

q.q: Why does a booking form for personal details use method="post"?
o: The data is sent in the body of the request rather than in the URL
The data is encrypted by the browser before it is sent
The data is checked against the database on the client
The data is posted to the user's email address as well
q.why: post keeps details out of the URL; encryption comes from HTTPS, not the method.

q.q: How is a label linked to its input so that screen readers announce it?
o: The label's id matches the input's name
The label is placed inside the input tag
The label's class matches the input's type
The label's for attribute matches the input's id
q.why: Matching for and id associates the label with the control.

q.q: In p { color: red; }, what is color?
o: A property
A value
The selector
An attribute
q.why: p is the selector, color the property and red its value.

q.q: Which selector applies to every element with class="note"?
o: #note
.note
note
*note
q.why: A full stop marks a class selector; a hash marks an id selector.

q.q: Which selector applies to the one element with id="banner"?
o: .banner
banner
#banner
id.banner
q.why: A hash marks an id selector; ids must be unique on a page.

q.q: What does the selector nav a apply to?
o: Links that are inside the nav element only
Every nav element and every link on the page
The first link that comes after a nav element
Elements that have the class nav or a
q.why: A descendant selector styles elements in context; a group selector uses a comma.

q.q: Which selector applies the same declarations to every h1 and every h2?
o: h1 h2
h1.h2
h1, h2
q.why: A comma groups selectors; a space would mean h2 elements inside h1 elements.

q.q: Which hex code is pure blue?
q.why: The last pair is blue at FF (255); the first pair is red and the middle green.

q.q: Which hex code is the same colour as rgb(0, 128, 0)?
q.why: 128 in denary is 80 in hexadecimal, so green is 00, 80, 00.

q.q: Which CSS rule correctly gives elements with class result navy Arial text on a light grey background?
o: #result { color: navy; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: #EEEEEE; }
.result { color: navy; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: #EEEEEE; }
.result { colour: navy; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-colour: #EEEEEE; }
.result { color = navy; font-family = Arial, sans-serif; background-color = #EEEEEE; }
q.why: Class selectors use a full stop, CSS spells color the American way, and each declaration uses a colon.

q.q: In h1 { font-family: Georgia, serif; }, why is serif listed after Georgia?
o: Both fonts are applied together, with serif used for capital letters
serif makes the Georgia text bold and slightly larger than normal
If Georgia is not available, the browser falls back to any serif font
The browser chooses one of the two fonts at random for each heading
q.why: The list gives fallbacks in order of preference.

q.q: Which style location affects every page that links to it?
o: An external style sheet
An inline style
An internal style sheet
The browser default
q.why: An external .css file is attached to each page with a link tag.

q.q: Where is an internal (global) style sheet placed?
o: In the style attribute of one element
In a separate .css file linked from every page
In a script block at the end of the body
In a style block in the head of one page
q.why: An internal sheet styles matching elements on that page only.

q.q: Why are inline styles hard to maintain on a large site?
o: They are stored in a separate file that every page must download
They apply to every page on the site, so one mistake spreads everywhere
They are repeated on every element and mix presentation into the content
They are ignored by most browsers unless an external sheet is present
q.why: Inline styles suit only quick one-off changes.

q.q: A p is set to Verdana, and a span inside it has no font set. What font is the span text?
o: Verdana, by inheritance
The browser default, as the span has no rule
Verdana, by precedence over the span
Times, as spans cannot inherit fonts
q.why: font-family is a text property, so the child inherits it from the parent.

q.q: The body text is green, a p rule says blue, and a span in that p has inline color: orange. What colour is the span?
o: Green
Blue
Black
Orange
q.why: The inline style is closest to the element and takes precedence.

q.q: Which property is NOT normally inherited by child elements?
o: font-size
border
color
font-family
q.why: Borders, padding and backgrounds belong only to the element they are set on.

q.q: An internal sheet has p { color: navy; font-family: Georgia; }. A p contains a span with style="color: crimson". How does the span text appear?
o: Navy Georgia
Crimson in the browser's default font
Crimson Georgia
Navy in the browser's default font
q.why: font-family is inherited from the p (Georgia); the inline color takes precedence over the inherited navy.

q.q: Two rules in external sheets set the colour of the same element with equally specific selectors. Which wins?
o: The rule that comes first
The rule with the shorter selector
Neither; the browser default is used
The rule that comes later
q.why: With equal specificity the later rule wins; a more specific selector, such as an id, would beat a less specific one.

q.q: What is the main benefit of an external style sheet for a large site?
o: It makes the HTML content unnecessary
One change updates every linked page
It stops browsers from caching pages
It hides content from search engines
q.why: One file controls the presentation of the whole site.

q.q: Why can an external style sheet make later pages load faster?
o: The browser caches the style sheet after downloading it once
The style sheet is compressed and stored inside each HTML file
The style sheet removes all images from the following pages
The style sheet is uploaded by FTP rather than sent by HTTP
q.why: The cached sheet is reused, and styles are not repeated in every page.

q.q: How does separating content and presentation help users on different devices?
o: The same HTML can be given different style rules for phones, large screens and print
Separate HTML pages are automatically written for each device that visits the site
Phones are prevented from loading the style sheet, so pages display more quickly
The content is duplicated so that each device receives its own complete copy
q.why: Only the presentation needs to change, for example using media queries.

q.q: How does separating HTML and CSS support the division of work?
o: Designers must approve each page before authors are allowed to add content
Every author writes their own internal style sheet for their own pages
The browser combines the work of authors and designers into one file
Content authors can write pages while designers work on the style sheet
q.why: The two jobs can go on independently without getting in each other's way.

q.q: Why is clean, semantic HTML with separate CSS better for accessibility and search?
o: Screen readers can only read pages that have no style sheet attached
Search engines rank pages higher if they contain more inline styles
Screen readers and crawlers can interpret meaning without formatting cluttering it
Crawlers download the CSS file to find out what each page is about
q.why: Meaning is clear when presentation is kept out of the markup.

q.q: A council site with 300 pages moves to one external style sheet. Which drawback should be weighed?
o: Every page will need to be edited whenever the brand colour changes
One mistake in the shared sheet affects every page, so it must be tested
Pages will become larger because the styles are repeated in each one
The site can no longer offer a high-contrast alternative style
q.why: The initial clean-up takes time, and a shared sheet means errors spread site-wide.

q.q: Which change is easier with a separate external style sheet than with styles mixed into the HTML?
o: Adding a new paragraph to one page
Changing the house colour across the whole site
Correcting a spelling mistake in a heading
Adding a new page to the site map
q.why: The colour is changed in one declaration in site.css rather than on every page.

q.q: What does a site map show?
o: The layout of one page, with annotations
The IP address of the web server
All the pages of a site and how they link
The CSS rules for each page
q.why: A site map is the structure of the whole site.

q.q: Why is a site map produced before a site is built?
o: So the structure and navigation are planned and no page is missed or unreachable
So the server's IP address can be registered with the DNS before launch
So the fonts, colours and alt text for every image can be agreed in detail
So the client can test the forms with valid, invalid and extreme data
q.why: Both parts are needed for full marks: what it shows and why it is produced.

q.q: What does a storyboard (wireframe) show?
o: All pages and the links between them
The order in which HTTP requests are sent
The tables in the site's database
The layout of each page, with annotations
q.why: Storyboards plan where the logo, menu, headings, text, images and form fields go.

q.q: Which detail would be added as an annotation on a storyboard?
o: The alt text for each image
The domain name registrar
The server's IP address
The test plan's expected results
q.why: Annotations add fonts, colours, link destinations, file names and alt text.

q.q: Which characteristic of the target audience should a developer find out?
o: The location of the web host
Their accessibility needs and the devices they use
The colour of the server cabinet
The time-to-live of DNS records
q.why: Age, interests, reading level, accessibility needs and devices shape the design.

q.q: A site is being designed for primary school pupils. Which design choice best fits this target audience?
o: Dense, precise information in small print
Long paragraphs of technical vocabulary
A command line for fast navigation
Large buttons, simple words and bright images
q.why: The audience decides the design; dense information suits accountants, not young children.

q.q: Why should storyboards or a clickable prototype be shown to the client and real users early?
o: The site cannot be hosted until users have approved it
Users must write the HTML for each page themselves
Problems are caught while they are still cheap to fix
It replaces the need to test the finished site
q.why: Mistakes found on paper are cheap to fix; mistakes found after launch are not.

q.q: What does an agreed house style later become?
o: The site map
The site's external style sheet
The test plan
The domain name
q.why: Agreed fonts, colours and logo position become the shared CSS.

q.q: Which navigation structure best suits an online checkout?
o: Hierarchical
Non-linear
Linear
Mesh
q.why: Steps must be completed in order using Next and Previous.

q.q: Which navigation structure is used by most organisational sites, such as schools and councils?
o: Linear
Non-linear
Sequential
Hierarchical
q.why: The home page links to main sections, each linking to its own sub-pages.

q.q: Which is a drawback of a non-linear structure?
o: Users can get lost and lose track of where they are
Users must follow a fixed order of pages
Deep trees need many clicks to reach a page
Pages cannot link to related pages
q.why: Free linking can disorient users; fixed order is a linear drawback.

q.q: Which is a drawback of a deep hierarchical structure?
o: Users must visit every page in a fixed order
Many clicks are needed to reach pages near the bottom
Pages can link freely, so users get lost
It cannot have a home page
q.why: Deep trees mean long paths from home to sub-pages.

q.q: A shop is browsed as Home, Women, Footwear, Boots and then paid for through Basket, Your details, Payment and Confirmation steps. Which statement is correct?
o: It combines a hierarchical structure for browsing with a linear structure for buying
It is entirely linear because each page leads on to the next
It is entirely non-linear because pages link to related items
It combines a linear structure for browsing with a hierarchical checkout
q.why: Most real sites combine structures.

q.q: What is responsive design?
o: A site that replies to users' emails automatically within a few minutes
A separate HTML version of the site written for every type of device
Flexible layouts and media queries that adapt the same content to each screen size
Server-side validation that responds instantly to every form entry
q.why: Content rearranges itself for phone, tablet and desktop without sideways scrolling.

q.q: Which feature improves usability?
o: Moving the menu to suit each page's content
Vague error messages shown at the top of the page
Large uncompressed images on the home page
Keeping the menu in the same place on every page
q.why: Consistent navigation helps users find their way.

q.q: Which error message best follows the usability principles in the notes?
o: 'Error 17', shown at the top of the page
'Enter a date after today', shown next to the date field
'Invalid input', shown after the form is cleared
'Something went wrong', shown in a pop-up
q.why: Helpful errors are specific and placed next to the problem field.

q.q: Who publishes the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)?
o: The ITU
The IETF
The W3C
Ofcom
q.why: WCAG is a W3C standard; the current version is WCAG 2.2.

q.q: What do the four WCAG principles, POUR, stand for?
o: Perceivable, operable, understandable, robust
Perceivable, organised, usable, readable
Portable, operable, understandable, responsive
Printable, operable, usable, robust
q.why: Success criteria are organised under these four principles.

q.q: Which WCAG principle covers making everything work by keyboard alone?
o: Perceivable
Understandable
Robust
Operable
q.why: Operable means every control can be used.

q.q: Which WCAG principle is met by using valid, semantic HTML so screen readers interpret it correctly?
o: Operable
Robust
Perceivable
Understandable
q.why: Robust content works reliably with assistive technology.

q.q: Captions and transcripts for video mainly help which users?
o: Users with epilepsy
Colour-blind users
Users on slow connections
Deaf or hard-of-hearing users
q.why: Captions make audio content perceivable.

q.q: Why should content not flash more than three times a second?
o: Flashing can trigger seizures in people with epilepsy
Flashing content cannot be read by crawlers
Flashing slows the page on mobile connections
Flashing breaks the layout when text is enlarged
q.why: This is an Operable criterion protecting people with epilepsy.

q.q: Which WCAG level must UK public sector websites meet?
o: A
AAA
AA
None
q.why: The Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018 require WCAG AA and an accessibility statement.

q.q: Which answer would gain marks for describing an accessibility feature?
o: The website should be made accessible so that blind people are able to use it
The website should be designed to be easy for everybody to use on any device
Alt text describes each image so a screen reader can read it aloud to a blind user
The website should follow the accessibility rules set out by the government
q.why: Name the specific feature, who it helps and how.

q.q: Plain language, labelled form fields and clear error messages fall under which WCAG principle?
o: Understandable
Perceivable
Operable
Robust
q.why: These help users with cognitive impairments or dyslexia and non-native speakers.

q.q: Which is a static web page?
o: An online banking statement
A seat booking page
A page of search results
A fixed 'About us' page stored as a file
q.why: A static page is retrieved and displayed unchanged.

q.q: What distinguishes a web application from a static web page?
o: It is stored on the server as a finished file and displayed unchanged
It processes what the user enters and usually keeps its state in a database
It is written only in HTML and needs no scripts on either side
It runs only on the user's device and never contacts the server
q.why: Web applications such as online banking change as people use them.

q.q: Which check can only be done server-side?
o: The username is not already taken
The date is in the correct format
The age is between 8 and 18
The password box is not empty
q.why: It needs the database, which only the server can reach.

q.q: Why does a booking system roll back the database if a card payment is declined?
o: So the server runs more quickly for the next customer
So the database stays consistent, for example no places are lost
So the user's account is deleted for security reasons
So the browser cache is cleared before the next attempt
q.why: No partial booking should remain.

q.q: What is the main benefit of client-side processing?
o: It updates the database as soon as each field is filled
It encrypts the data before it leaves the device
It cannot be bypassed by the user in any way
Instant feedback without a round trip, reducing server load
q.why: Speed and reduced load are the benefits; it can be bypassed.

q.q: When signing in to a credit union's online banking, which step is server-side?
o: Checking both boxes are filled in
Checking the member number is the right length
Checking the password against the stored hashed value
Showing a message if a box is empty
q.why: Comparing with the stored record needs the database on the server.

q.q: A server-side booking script receives a request to reserve two places. What does it normally do next?
o: Check that the form fields are not empty in the browser
Send the database to the browser for checking
Ask the user to reload the page
Fetch the number of places left from the database
q.why: It fetches what it needs, computes, writes back, handles payment and builds a response page.

q.q: Why is server-side processing essential for confidential data?
o: The database and code stay on the server where users cannot see or alter them
The browser cannot display confidential data unless the server builds it
Server-side scripts run faster than any code in the browser
Client-side scripts cannot send any data to the web server
q.why: Users control the client, so shared or confidential data must be handled on the server.

q.q: Which HTML attribute acts as a presence check?
o: pattern
maxlength
required
min
q.why: required stops a blank field being submitted.

q.q: Which HTML attribute performs a format check?
o: required
pattern
max
alt
q.why: pattern tests input against a regular expression, e.g. two letters then four digits.

q.q: Which validation check do min and max attributes perform?
o: Length check
Range check
Presence check
Format check
q.why: For example, an age from 8 to 18.

q.q: A membership number input has pattern="[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4}". Which value would be accepted?
o: EN123
EN12A4
q.why: Exactly two capital letters then four digits; a letter among the digits or a wrong length fails.

q.q: Why must data validated in the browser be validated again on the server?
o: HTML has no way of validating any data entered in a form
Browsers are too slow to validate long forms before sending
Client-side checks can be bypassed, so the server must protect the database
Servers cannot store data unless they have validated it twice
q.why: Users control the client.

q.q: Which is a way a user could bypass client-side validation?
o: Edit the page with developer tools to remove the required attribute
Use HTTPS so that the validation is encrypted
Fill in every field with data in the correct format
Clear the browser's cache before submitting
q.why: Scripts can be switched off, attributes removed, or requests sent straight to the server.

q.q: Which check can only be done on the server?
o: Is the age a number?
Is the postcode 8 characters or fewer?
Is this email address already registered?
Is the email field filled in?
q.why: It requires looking in the database.

q.q: A user types the password twice so the two entries can be compared. What is this?
o: Validation
A range check
A format check
Verification
q.why: Verification checks data was entered accurately; validation checks it is reasonable.

q.q: A validated date of birth is accepted but is the wrong date. Why?
o: Validation was done on the client rather than the server
Validation only checks data is reasonable, not that it is correct
The pattern attribute only works for text fields
Range checks cannot be applied to dates
q.why: Validation cannot prove data is correct.

q.q: What is a broken link?
o: A link whose destination does not exist, giving an error such as 404
A link to an email address that opens a new message
A link that opens its destination in a new tab
A link that uses HTTPS rather than plain HTTP
q.why: Broken links point to missing pages and are found by link testing.

q.q: What is compatibility testing?
o: Checking the HTML and CSS against W3C standards with a validator
Checking pages display and work in different browsers and on different devices
Checking that real users can complete tasks without any help
Checking that the home page loads in under three seconds
q.why: The others are code validation, usability and performance tests.

q.q: An age field accepts 8 to 18. Which pair of test data is extreme (boundary) data?
o: 7 and 19
12 and 13
8 and 18
q.why: Extreme data lies on the boundary of what should be accepted; 7 and 19 are invalid data.

q.q: Which is a well-written test from a test plan?
o: Check that the booking form works properly with different data
Make sure the site looks good on all phones and computers
Enter age 19 → message 'Age must be 8 to 18' shown next to the field
Test the links to see if they are all working correctly
q.why: Good tests name the test data and the expected result.

q.q: Which protocol is commonly used to upload a site's files to its host?
o: FTP or SFTP
HTTP
DNS
SMTP
q.why: FTP and SFTP transfer files to servers; the host's control panel is an alternative.

q.q: Why must the domain's DNS records be updated when publishing a site?
o: So the HTML and CSS can be validated against standards
So the site's files are compressed before they are uploaded
So the storyboards can be shared with the client
So the domain name resolves to the host server's IP address
q.why: Without DNS pointing at the host, the name leads nowhere.

q.q: What is the correct order for publishing a website?
o: Register domain, rent hosting, upload files, point DNS, install TLS certificate, retest
Upload files, register domain, install TLS certificate, rent hosting, point DNS, retest
Rent hosting, point DNS, register domain, upload files, retest, install TLS certificate
Register domain, point DNS, install TLS certificate, upload files, rent hosting, retest

q.q: A club has registered a domain name. Why is its site still not online?
o: The domain must first be validated by the W3C before it can be used
Registering a name does not store the site anywhere; it must also be hosted
Domain names only work once the site has a high PageRank
The TLS certificate must be renewed before the name is active
q.why: A domain name is not the same as hosting.

o: Drawing the site map for the first time
Choosing the target audience
Renewing the domain and TLS certificate before they expire
